newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan develops new brake-assist system.
newsitem.headline: Nissan develops new brake-assist system.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it developed a new brake-assist system that enhances emergency braking but does not interfere with braking in ordinary driving conditions.
Nissan will introduce the new system in combination with an anti-lock braking system (ABS) in a new car scheduled for launch this spring.
Nissan plans to include the brake-assist system in nearly all of its cars and recreational vehicles by the end of 1999.
The new brake booster increases braking force by about 50 percent during emergency stops, Nissan said.
Unlike existing brake-assist systems, however, Nissan's two-stage mechanical system will not affect braking in ordinary driving conditions, the company said.
Mercedes-Benz already offers electronic brake-assist systems in its S-Class and SL sports cars.
